q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Tenth World Hindi Conference (Vishwa Hindi Sammelan) was held in the year 2015 at Bhopal.
2. The Eleventh World Hindi Conference was held in the year 2018 at Port Louis (Mauritius).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Tenth World Hindi Conference was held in 2015 at Bhopal and the Eleventh in 2018 at Port Louis, Mauritius. Both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Eighth World Hindi Conference was held in the year 2007 at New York.
2. The Fifth World Hindi Conference was held in the year 1996 at London.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Eighth World Hindi Conference was held in 2007 at New York. The Fifth Conference in 1996 was held at Port of Spain, Trinidad and Tobago, not London, so only statement 1 is correct.

q: Which of the following pairs of a State/Union Territory and the Region in which it is placed under the Official Language Rules, 1976 is NOT correctly matched?

options.B: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu — Region 'B'

e: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, Punjab is placed in Region B, not Region A. Haryana is in Region A, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu in Region B, so pair D is the incorrectly matched one.

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes Article 345 from Article 347 of the Constitution?

options.A: Article 345 empowers the Legislature of a State to adopt one or more languages in use in the State, or Hindi, as the official language of that State, while Article 347 empowers the President to direct that a language spoken by a substantial proportion of the population of a State shall also be officially recognised for specified purposes
options.B: Article 345 deals with the recognition of a language on a direction of the President, while Article 347 deals with the official language of a State
options.C: Both the Articles deal only with the language to be used in the Supreme Court and the High Courts
options.D: Article 345 deals with the development of Hindi, while Article 347 deals with instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage

e: Article 345 empowers a State Legislature to adopt one or more languages in use in the State, or Hindi, as the official language of the State, while Article 347 empowers the President to direct official recognition of a language spoken by a substantial proportion of the population for specified purposes.

q: A Hindi-speaking passenger approaches the enquiry counter of a railway station with a query and the railway staff at the counter attend to him only in English. The correct position is that the staff should, as far as possible, attend to him:

options.A: Only in English, enquiries being official work
options.C: Only in the regional language of the State
options.D: After calling an interpreter from the Rajbhasha section

e: Rajbhasha instructions require staff at public dealing counters, including railway enquiry counters, to attend to a Hindi-speaking person in Hindi as far as possible.

q: A Central Government office issues a notification in English only, on the ground that the persons concerned are all English-knowing officers. Under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the correct position is that the notification is required to be issued in:

options.A: English only, as issued by the office
options.D: English, with a Hindi summary attached at the end

e: Notifications are among the documents listed in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, and must be issued in both Hindi and English regardless of who the recipients are.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Constitution of India does not declare any language as the national language of India.
2. After the amendment of the Official Languages Act in 1967, English continues to be used for the official purposes of the Union as an associate official language, in addition to Hindi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Constitution declares no language as the national language; Hindi is the official language of the Union. After the 1967 amendment to the Official Languages Act, English continues as an associate official language in addition to Hindi. Both are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Maithili language is mainly spoken in the Mithila region of the State of Bihar.
2. The Dogri language is mainly spoken in the Kashmir valley.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Maithili is spoken mainly in the Mithila region of Bihar. Dogri is spoken mainly in the Jammu region, not the Kashmir valley, so only statement 1 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Sanskrit has been declared as the second official language of the State of Uttarakhand.
2. Besides Uttarakhand, Sanskrit has also been declared as the second official language of the State of Himachal Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Sanskrit has been declared the second official language of Uttarakhand, and Himachal Pradesh has also declared Sanskrit as its second official language. Both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Memorandum" is Gyapan.
2. The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Office Memorandum" is Karyalaya Gyapan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: In the standard administrative glossary, Memorandum and Office Memorandum are rendered by their standard Hindi equivalents stated in the two statements, as used in official correspondence. Both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 346 of the Constitution, the language for the time being authorised for use in the Union for its official purposes shall be the official language for communication between the Union and a State, or between one State and another.
2. Under Section 8 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act vests in the Central Government.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Article 346 makes the language authorised for official purposes of the Union the language for communication between the Union and a State and between States, and Section 8 of the Official Languages Act, 1963 vests rule-making power in the Central Government. Both are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 351 of the Constitution, Hindi shall draw for its vocabulary primarily on Sanskrit and secondarily on other languages.
2. The Official Language Commission to be constituted under Article 344 of the Constitution consists of a Chairman and other members representing the different languages specified in the Eighth Schedule.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Article 351 directs that Hindi draw its vocabulary primarily on Sanskrit and secondarily on other languages, and the Article 344 Commission consists of a Chairman and members representing the different languages of the Eighth Schedule. Both are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Official Languages Act, 1963 came into force on 26th January, 1965.
2. The Official Languages (Use for Official Purposes of the Union) Rules were framed in the year 1976.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Official Languages Act, 1963 came into force on 26 January 1965, and the Official Languages (Use for Official Purposes of the Union) Rules were framed in 1976. Both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Of the 30 members of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language, 20 are drawn from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha.
2. The Parliamentary Committee on Official Language was constituted in the year 1976.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Committee of Parliament on Official Language has 30 members - 20 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha - and it was constituted in 1976 under Section 4 of the 1963 Act. Both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Hindi Diwas was celebrated for the first time in the year 1953.
2. World Hindi Day, observed on 10th January every year, was observed for the first time in the year 2006.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Hindi Diwas was first celebrated in 1953, marking 14 September 1949 when Hindi was adopted as the official language, and World Hindi Day on 10 January was first observed in 2006. Both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, 1976, the State of Haryana is placed in Region 'A'.
2. For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, 1976, the State of Karnataka is placed in Region 'B'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Haryana is in Region A under the Official Language Rules, 1976. Karnataka is in Region C, not Region B, so only statement 1 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, 1976, the State of Rajasthan is placed in Region 'A'.
2. For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, 1976, the State of Kerala is placed in Region 'C'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Rajasthan is placed in Region A and Kerala in Region C under the Official Language Rules, 1976. Both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The official language of the State of Chhattisgarh is Hindi.
2. The official language of the State of Telangana is Hindi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The official language of Chhattisgarh is Hindi. The official language of Telangana is Telugu (with Urdu as second official language), not Hindi, so only statement 1 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The official language of the State of Nagaland is English.
2. The official language of the State of Meghalaya is English.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: English is the official language of both Nagaland and Meghalaya. Both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Urdu has been declared as the second official language of the State of Bihar.
2. Urdu has been declared as the second official language of the State of Uttar Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Urdu has been declared the second official language in both Bihar and Uttar Pradesh for specified purposes. Both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Tamil was the first language to be declared a 'classical language' by the Government of India.
2. Odia was accorded the status of a 'classical language' by the Government of India in the year 2014.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Tamil was the first language declared a classical language by the Government of India in 2004, and Odia was accorded classical language status in 2014. Both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements, with reference to the Census of India, 2011:
1. Marathi is the third most widely spoken language (mother tongue) in India.
2. Telugu is the fourth most widely spoken language (mother tongue) in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: As per Census 2011 mother tongue figures, Hindi is first, Bengali second, Marathi third and Telugu fourth among the most widely spoken languages in India. Both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Sahitya Akademi, India's national academy of letters, was established in the year 1954.
2. International Mother Language Day is observed every year on 21st February.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Sahitya Akademi was established in 1954 as India national academy of letters, and International Mother Language Day is observed on 21 February every year. Both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The first Hindi daily newspaper, 'Samachar Sudha Varshan', was published in the year 1854 from Calcutta.
2. 'Alam Ara', the first Indian talkie film released in the year 1931, was made in the Hindi language.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Samachar Sudha Varshan, published from Calcutta in 1854, is regarded as the first Hindi daily newspaper, and Alam Ara of 1931 was the first Indian talkie, made in Hindi. Both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The celebrated Hindi magazine 'Hans' was founded by Munshi Premchand.
2. The celebrated Hindi magazine 'Saraswati' was first published in the year 1910.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The magazine Hans was founded by Munshi Premchand in 1930. Saraswati was first published in 1900, not 1910, so only statement 1 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The real name of Munshi Premchand, the celebrated Hindi novelist, was Dhanpat Rai Srivastava.
2. The first recipient of the Jnanpith Award, in the year 1965, was G. Sankara Kurup.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Munshi Premchand real name was Dhanpat Rai Srivastava, and G. Sankara Kurup was the first recipient of the Jnanpith Award in 1965. Both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The first Hindi writer to receive the Jnanpith Award was Sumitranandan Pant.
2. The first woman writer to receive the Jnanpith Award was Ashapurna Devi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Sumitranandan Pant was the first Hindi writer to receive the Jnanpith Award, and Ashapurna Devi was the first woman writer to receive it. Both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. 'Pariksha Guru' (1882), regarded as the first novel in Hindi, was written by Lala Srinivas Das.
2. 'Indumati', published in the year 1900 and regarded as the first short story in Hindi, was written by Kishorilal Goswami.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Pariksha Guru (1882) by Lala Srinivas Das is regarded as the first Hindi novel, and Indumati (1900) by Kishorilal Goswami is regarded as the first Hindi short story. Both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Kashmiri language belongs to the Dardic group of the Indo-Aryan family of languages.
2. The Santhali language, included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, belongs to the Austroasiatic (Munda) family of languages.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Kashmiri belongs to the Dardic group of the Indo-Aryan family, and Santhali, an Eighth Schedule language, belongs to the Austroasiatic (Munda) family. Both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Marathi does not belong to the Dravidian family of languages.
2. The Bhojpuri language belongs to the Bihari group of languages/dialects.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Marathi is an Indo-Aryan language, not a Dravidian language, and Bhojpuri belongs to the Bihari group of languages. Both statements are correct, the first being a correct negative statement.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Bagheli dialect belongs to the Eastern Hindi group of Hindi dialects.
2. The Chhattisgarhi dialect belongs to the Western Hindi group of Hindi dialects.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Bagheli belongs to the Eastern Hindi group of dialects. Chhattisgarhi also belongs to the Eastern Hindi group, not the Western Hindi group, so only statement 1 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Assamese language belongs to the Eastern group of the Indo-Aryan family of languages.
2. The Sanskrit language, included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, has no separate script of its own and is generally written in the Devanagari script.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Assamese belongs to the Eastern group of the Indo-Aryan family, and Sanskrit has no separate script of its own and is generally written in Devanagari. Both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Gujarati script, though derived from Devanagari, has the headstroke (shirorekha) like the Devanagari script.
2. The script of the Malayalam language has evolved from the ancient script known as Grantha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Gujarati script, though derived from Devanagari, does not have the headstroke found in Devanagari, so statement 1 is false. The Malayalam script evolved from the ancient Grantha script, so only statement 2 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the State of Karnataka, the Konkani language is generally written in the Devanagari script.
2. In Pakistan, the Punjabi language is written in the Gurmukhi script.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: In Karnataka, Konkani is generally written in the Kannada script, not Devanagari, and in Pakistan Punjabi is written in the Shahmukhi script, not Gurmukhi. Both statements are false, so neither is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Travelling Allowance" is Yatra Bhatta.
2. The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Dearness Allowance" is Mahangai Bhatta.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: In standard administrative terminology, Travelling Allowance and Dearness Allowance are rendered by the standard Hindi equivalents stated in the two statements. Both are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, 1976, the expression "Central Government office" includes an office of a company or corporation owned or controlled by the Central Government.
2. The Official Languages Act, 1963 extends to the whole of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The definition of Central Government office in the Official Language Rules, 1976 includes an office of a company or corporation owned or controlled by the Central Government, and the Official Languages Act, 1963 extends to the whole of India. Both are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Eighth Schedule of the Constitution is referred to in Articles 344 and 351 of the Constitution.
2. At the commencement of the Constitution, the Eighth Schedule contained 22 languages.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Eighth Schedule is referred to in Articles 344 and 351 of the Constitution. At the commencement of the Constitution it contained 14 languages, not 22, so only statement 1 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Central Hindi Training Institute, New Delhi was established in the year 1960.
2. The Kendriya Hindi Sansthan (Central Institute of Hindi) at Agra was established in the year 1960.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Kendriya Hindi Sansthan at Agra was established in 1960. The Central Hindi Training Institute at New Delhi was established much later, in 1985, not 1960, so only statement 2 is correct.

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes Section 5 from Section 7 of the Official Languages Act, 1963?

options.A: Section 5 deals with the Committee of Parliament on Official Language, while Section 7 deals with the rule-making power of the Central Government
options.B: Section 5 provides that the Hindi translation of a Central Act or Ordinance, published under the authority of the President in the Official Gazette, shall be deemed to be the authoritative text thereof in Hindi, while Section 7 provides for the use of Hindi, or the official language of a State, in addition to English, for judgments, decrees or orders of a High Court, on authorisation by the Governor with the previous consent of the President
options.C: Both the Sections deal only with the documents to be issued in both Hindi and English
options.D: Section 5 deals with the use of Hindi in judgments of High Courts, while Section 7 deals with the authoritative Hindi text of Central Acts

e: Section 5 of the 1963 Act makes the published Hindi translation of a Central Act or Ordinance the authoritative Hindi text, while Section 7 provides for use of Hindi or the State official language, in addition to English, for High Court judgments on authorisation by the Governor with the President previous consent.

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes Article 348 from Article 349 of the Constitution?

options.A: Article 348 deals with the development of Hindi, while Article 349 deals with instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage
options.B: Both the Articles deal only with the official language of the States
options.C: Article 348 lays down that the language of the Supreme Court and the High Courts, and the authoritative texts of Bills, Acts, orders, rules, regulations and bye-laws, shall be English until Parliament by law otherwise provides, while Article 349 lays down a special procedure for the enactment of certain laws relating to the language to be used in the Supreme Court and the High Courts
options.D: Article 348 empowers the President to direct the recognition of a language spoken by a substantial proportion of the population of a State, while Article 349 empowers a State Legislature to adopt the official language of the State

e: Article 348 provides that the language of the Supreme Court and High Courts and of authoritative texts of Bills, Acts, orders, rules, regulations and bye-laws shall be English until Parliament by law otherwise provides, while Article 349 prescribes a special procedure for enacting laws on that court language.

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Central Hindi Directorate from the Central Translation Bureau?

options.A: The Central Hindi Directorate translates codes, manuals, forms and other non-statutory material, while the Central Translation Bureau conducts the correspondence courses in Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya
options.B: Both the bodies only conduct the Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya examinations
options.C: Both the bodies function only at the level of Zonal Railways
options.D: The Central Hindi Directorate conducts the correspondence courses in Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya for employees who cannot attend regular classes and prepared the standard form of the Devanagari script and of Hindi spelling (Manak Vartani), while the Central Translation Bureau is mainly responsible for the translation of codes, manuals, forms and other non-statutory material of Central Government offices

e: The Central Hindi Directorate conducts the Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya correspondence courses and prepared the standard Devanagari script form and standard Hindi spelling, while the Central Translation Bureau mainly translates codes, manuals, forms and other non-statutory material of Central Government offices.

q: Which one of the following statements relating to the World Hindi Conferences is FALSE?

options.A: The First World Hindi Conference was held in the year 1975 at Nagpur
options.B: The Second World Hindi Conference was held in the year 1976 at Port Louis (Mauritius)
options.C: The Tenth World Hindi Conference was held in the year 2015 at Bhopal
options.D: The Eleventh World Hindi Conference was held in the year 2018 at New Delhi

e: The Eleventh World Hindi Conference was held in 2018 at Port Louis, Mauritius, not New Delhi. The statements about the First (1975, Nagpur), Second (1976, Port Louis) and Tenth (2015, Bhopal) conferences are correct, so D is false.

q: Which one of the following statements relating to the committees for the implementation of the Official Language Policy is FALSE?

options.A: The Committee of Parliament on Official Language consists of 30 members
options.B: The Kendriya Hindi Samiti (Central Hindi Committee), the highest policy-making body for the progressive use of Hindi, is chaired by the Prime Minister
options.C: The Official Language Implementation Committee of a Central Government office is chaired by the head of the office
options.D: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee is chaired by the District Magistrate of the town

e: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee is chaired by the senior-most Central Government officer in the town, not the District Magistrate. The other statements on the Parliamentary Committee (30 members), Kendriya Hindi Samiti and office implementation committees are correct, so D is false.

q: A Central Government office finalises tender forms and a notice inviting tenders and proposes to issue them in Hindi only, on the ground that Hindi is the Official Language of the Union. Under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the correct position is that tender forms and notices inviting tenders are required to be issued in:

options.A: Hindi only, as proposed by the office
options.D: The regional language of the State where the office is located

e: Tender forms and notices inviting tenders are listed in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, and must be issued in both Hindi and English, not in Hindi only.

q: A Central Government office has to issue a licence (permit) to an applicant and proposes to issue it in English only, on the ground that the applicant is an English-knowing firm. Under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the correct position is that the licence or permit is required to be issued in:

options.A: English only, as proposed by the office
options.C: The regional language of the State where the office is located

e: Licences and permits are listed in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, and must be issued in both Hindi and English, irrespective of the applicant.

q: An Act passed by the Legislature of a State in a language other than Hindi is translated into Hindi, and the translation is published in the Official Gazette of the State under the authority of the President. Under Section 6 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, that translation shall be deemed to be:

options.A: A mere unofficial summary of the Act
options.B: The authoritative text thereof in Hindi
options.D: A draft requiring the approval of Parliament

e: Under Section 6 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the Hindi translation of a State Act passed in a language other than Hindi, published in the State Official Gazette under the authority of the President, is deemed the authoritative text thereof in Hindi.

q: A substantial proportion of the population of a State desires that a language spoken by them should be recognised by the State. The President is satisfied in this regard and directs that the language shall also be officially recognised for specified purposes in a part of that State. This direction is issued under:
e: Article 347 empowers the President, on being satisfied that a substantial proportion of a State population desires it, to direct official recognition of their language for specified purposes in the whole or part of the State.

q: At a railway station, announcements for the guidance of passengers are made only in Hindi and English, the regional language of the area being omitted altogether. Under the Official Language Policy, the correct position is that such announcements are required to be made in:

options.A: Hindi and English only, as is being done at the station
options.D: Three languages — the regional language, Hindi and English

e: Under the trilingual arrangement for passenger amenities, announcements at railway stations must be made in three languages - the regional language, Hindi and English - and omitting the regional language is not permitted.

q: An employee passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 67 per cent marks. The cash award admissible to him is:
e: Under the Hindi Teaching Scheme cash award slabs for Pragya, marks in the 60 to 69 per cent slab earn Rs 1,600; 67 per cent falls in that slab.

q: An employee passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 57 per cent marks. The cash award admissible to him is:
e: Under the Hindi Teaching Scheme cash award slabs for Pragya, marks in the 55 to 59 per cent slab earn Rs 800; 57 per cent falls in that slab.

q: An employee passes the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 91 per cent marks. In this case:

options.A: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 95 per cent marks
options.B: A cash award is admissible only if he also passes the Hindi stenography examination
options.C: He becomes entitled to personal pay for a period of 24 months
options.D: A cash award is admissible to him, the prescribed threshold for the typewriting examination being 90 per cent or more marks

e: Under the Hindi Teaching Scheme, a cash award for the Hindi typewriting examination is admissible on securing 90 per cent or more marks; 91 per cent crosses that threshold.

q: An employee passes the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 92 per cent marks. In this case:

options.A: A cash award is admissible to him, the prescribed threshold for the stenography examination being 88 per cent or more marks
options.B: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 95 per cent marks
options.C: A cash award is admissible only if he also passes the Hindi typewriting examination
options.D: He becomes entitled to a lumpsum award

e: Under the Hindi Teaching Scheme, a cash award for the Hindi stenography examination is admissible on securing 88 per cent or more marks; 92 per cent crosses that threshold.

q: An employee aged 43 years, who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi, is nominated for in-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme. The correct position is:

options.A: He is exempt, in-service Hindi training not being compulsory after the age of 40 years
options.B: He must undergo the training only if his office is located in Region 'A'
options.C: He must undergo the training, in-service Hindi training being compulsory for an employee who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi and has not attained the age of 45 years
options.D: He must undergo the training on payment of the prescribed fee

e: In-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is compulsory for an employee who lacks working knowledge of Hindi and has not attained 45 years; at 43 years the employee must undergo it.

q: In a Central Government office, 88 per cent of the staff have acquired working knowledge of Hindi. The correct position regarding notification of the office under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976 is:

options.A: The office cannot be notified, as notification requires more than 90 per cent of the staff to have acquired working knowledge of Hindi
options.B: The office can be notified, the prescribed proportion being 80 per cent or more of the staff having acquired working knowledge of Hindi
options.C: The office cannot be notified, as notification depends on the total number of staff and not on any proportion
options.D: The office can be notified only during Hindi Pakhwada

e: Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976 permits notification of an office where 80 per cent or more of the staff have acquired working knowledge of Hindi; at 88 per cent the office can be notified.

q: An employee does noting and drafting in Hindi of 15,000 words during a year and claims consideration for a cash award under the incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi. The correct position is:

options.A: He is not eligible, the prescribed minimum being 50,000 words in a year
options.B: He is eligible only if he has also passed the Pragya examination with 70 per cent or more marks
options.C: He becomes eligible for consideration for the cash award, the prescribed minimum being at least 10,000 words of noting and drafting in Hindi in a year
options.D: He is eligible only if his office is notified under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976

e: Under the incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi, the prescribed minimum is at least 10,000 words in a year; 15,000 words makes the employee eligible for consideration for the cash award.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 343 of the Constitution, the numerals to be used for the official purposes of the Union are the international form of Indian numerals.
2. The Kendriya Hindi Samiti (Central Hindi Committee) was set up in the year 1967.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Article 343(1) provides that the numerals to be used for official purposes of the Union shall be the international form of Indian numerals, and the Kendriya Hindi Samiti was set up in 1967. Both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 120 of the Constitution, business in Parliament shall be transacted in Hindi or in English.
2. Under Article 29 of the Constitution, any section of the citizens residing in India having a distinct language, script or culture of its own shall have the right to conserve the same.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Article 120 provides that business in Parliament shall be transacted in Hindi or in English, and Article 29(1) gives any section of citizens with a distinct language, script or culture the right to conserve it. Both are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Section 3(2) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the English language shall be used for communication between the Union and a State which has not adopted Hindi as its official language.
2. The Annual Programme for the progressive use of Hindi, containing the targets to be achieved by Central Government offices, is issued by the Department of Official Language every year.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Section 3(2) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 provides for use of English in communication between the Union and a State that has not adopted Hindi as its official language, and the Annual Programme with targets for progressive use of Hindi is issued every year by the Department of Official Language. Both are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Fort William College at Calcutta, associated with the development of Hindi prose, was established in the year 1800 by Lord Wellesley.
2. The headquarters of the Hindi Sahitya Sammelan, a leading organisation for the promotion of Hindi, is located at Prayagraj.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Fort William College at Calcutta was established in 1800 by Lord Wellesley and is associated with the development of Hindi prose, and the Hindi Sahitya Sammelan has its headquarters at Prayagraj. Both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements, with reference to the Census of India, 2011:
1. The number of languages each spoken by 10,000 or more persons is 121.
2. Among the languages included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, Sanskrit has the smallest number of speakers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Census 2011 records 121 languages each spoken by 10,000 or more persons, and among Eighth Schedule languages Sanskrit has the smallest number of speakers. Both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 344 of the Constitution, in making its recommendations, the Official Language Commission shall have due regard to the industrial, cultural and scientific advancement of India and the just claims and interests of persons belonging to the non-Hindi speaking areas in respect of public services.
2. Under Article 351 of the Constitution, it shall be the duty of the Union to promote the spread of the Hindi language and to develop it so that it may serve as a medium of expression for all the elements of the composite culture of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Article 344 requires the Official Language Commission to have due regard to the industrial, cultural and scientific advancement of India and the just claims of non-Hindi speaking areas in public services, and Article 351 makes it the duty of the Union to promote the spread and development of Hindi as a medium for the composite culture. Both are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the Jammu and Kashmir Official Languages Act, 2020, the number of languages declared as the official languages of the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir is five.
2. Dogri is one of the official languages of the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir under that Act.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Jammu and Kashmir Official Languages Act, 2020 declares five official languages for the Union Territory, and Dogri is one of them, along with Kashmiri, Urdu, Hindi and English. Both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, 1976, the Union Territory of Ladakh is placed in Region 'C'.
2. Hindi is one of the official languages of the Union Territory of Ladakh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, 1976, Ladakh is placed in Region C, and Hindi is one of the official languages of the Union Territory of Ladakh. Both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the Official Language Act of Goa, besides Konkani, the official language of the State, Marathi may also be used for all or any of the official purposes of the State.
2. For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, 1976, the State of Goa is placed in Region 'C'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Under the Goa official language law, Konkani is the official language of Goa and Marathi may also be used for all or any official purposes of the State, and Goa is placed in Region C under the Official Language Rules, 1976. Both are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The official language of the Union Territory of Puducherry is Tamil.
2. For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, 1976, the Union Territory of Puducherry is placed in Region 'C'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Tamil is the official language of the Union Territory of Puducherry, and Puducherry is placed in Region C under the Official Language Rules, 1976. Both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. With the additions made in October 2024, the total number of languages recognised as 'classical languages' in India has become eleven.
2. Prakrit was among the languages accorded the status of a 'classical language' in October 2024.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: With the five additions of October 2024, the total number of classical languages in India became eleven, and Prakrit was one of the languages accorded classical status in that round. Both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Section 4 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the members of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language are elected by the members of the two Houses of Parliament in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.
2. Under Section 4 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the report of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language is submitted to the President, who shall cause it to be laid before each House of Parliament and sent to all the State Governments.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Section 4 of the Official Languages Act, 1963 provides that members of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language are elected by members of both Houses by proportional representation through the single transferable vote, and that its report goes to the President, who causes it to be laid before Parliament and sent to all State Governments. Both are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Hindi workshops (Hindi Karyashala) are organised in Central Government offices primarily to give employees who possess knowledge of Hindi practical training in doing noting, drafting and other official work in Hindi.
2. The standard keyboard layout adopted for Hindi (Devanagari) typing on computers in Central Government offices is known as InScript.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Hindi workshops give employees who know Hindi practical training in noting, drafting and other official work in Hindi, and InScript is the standard keyboard layout adopted for Devanagari typing on computers in Central Government offices. Both are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The office of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities was set up in the year 1957.
2. The headquarters of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities is located at Prayagraj (Allahabad).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The office of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities was set up in 1957 under Article 350B, and its headquarters is located at Prayagraj. Both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Central Hindi Directorate functions under the Ministry of Education.
2. The Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology functions under the Ministry of Education.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Central Hindi Directorate and the Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology both function under the Ministry of Education. Both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The authorisation given by the Governor, with the previous consent of the President, under Article 348(2) of the Constitution for the use of Hindi in the proceedings of a High Court does not extend to any judgment, decree or order of that High Court.
2. Where the use of Hindi for judgments, decrees or orders of a High Court has been authorised under Section 7 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, every such judgment, decree or order shall be accompanied by a translation thereof in English issued under the authority of the High Court.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The Article 348(2) authorisation for Hindi in High Court proceedings expressly does not extend to judgments, decrees or orders, and Section 7 of the 1963 Act requires every judgment, decree or order issued in Hindi or the State language to be accompanied by an English translation issued under the authority of the High Court. Both are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In-service Hindi training was made compulsory for Central Government employees by the Presidential Order of 1960.
2. The training imparted to Central Government employees under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is free of cost during office hours, the training period being treated as on duty.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: In-service Hindi training was made compulsory for Central Government employees by the Presidential Order of 1960, and training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is free of cost during office hours with the period treated as on duty. Both are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. To ensure that the documents specified in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 are invariably issued in both Hindi and English, certain points in a Central Government office, such as the despatch section, are designated as 'Check Points'.
2. 'Rajbhasha Bharati', the quarterly journal devoted to the Official Language and its implementation, is published by the Department of Official Language.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Check Points, such as the despatch section, are designated in Central Government offices to ensure Section 3(3) documents are invariably issued in both Hindi and English, and Rajbhasha Bharati, the quarterly journal on Official Language implementation, is published by the Department of Official Language. Both are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 394A of the Constitution, which provides for the authoritative text of the Constitution in the Hindi language, was inserted by the Constitution (58th Amendment) Act, 1987.
2. Article 343 of the Constitution, which declares Hindi in the Devanagari script as the Official Language of the Union, is contained in Chapter I of Part XVII of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Article 394A on the authoritative Hindi text of the Constitution was inserted by the Constitution (58th Amendment) Act, 1987, and Article 343 declaring Hindi in Devanagari script as the official language of the Union is in Chapter I of Part XVII. Both are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. At the commencement of the Constitution, the Eighth Schedule contained 14 languages.
2. After the inclusion of Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali in the Eighth Schedule in the year 1992, the total number of languages included in the Schedule became 18.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: At the commencement of the Constitution the Eighth Schedule contained 14 languages, and after Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali were included in 1992 the total became 18. Both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The headquarters of the World Hindi Secretariat (Vishwa Hindi Sachivalaya) is located in Mauritius.
2. 'Sarnami', a form of Hindi spoken by the Indian diaspora, is spoken mainly in Suriname.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The World Hindi Secretariat has its headquarters in Mauritius, and Sarnami, a form of Hindi spoken by the Indian diaspora, is spoken mainly in Suriname. Both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The word 'Urdu' is derived from a Turkish word which means an army or army camp.
2. 'Rekhta' was the earlier name by which the Urdu language was commonly known.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The word Urdu is derived from a Turkish word meaning an army or army camp, and Rekhta was the earlier name by which Urdu was commonly known. Both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Bharatendu Harishchandra is regarded as the father of modern Hindi literature.
2. The celebrated Hindi magazine 'Saraswati' was edited for a long period by Mahavir Prasad Dwivedi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Bharatendu Harishchandra is regarded as the father of modern Hindi literature, and the magazine Saraswati was edited for a long period by Mahavir Prasad Dwivedi. Both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The United Nations has six official languages.
2. Fiji Hindi is one of the official languages of Fiji.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The United Nations has six official languages, and Fiji Hindi is one of the official languages of Fiji. Both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. 'Thirukkural', the celebrated classical work in Tamil, was authored by Thiruvalluvar.
2. Rabindranath Tagore's 'Gitanjali' was originally written in the Bengali language.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Thirukkural, the celebrated Tamil classical work, was authored by Thiruvalluvar, and Rabindranath Tagore Gitanjali was originally written in Bengali. Both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The official language of the State of Arunachal Pradesh is English.
2. The official language of the State of Mizoram is Hindi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The official language of Arunachal Pradesh is English. The official language of Mizoram is Mizo (with English for official purposes), not Hindi, so only statement 1 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The official language of the State of Haryana is Punjabi.
2. The official language of the State of Himachal Pradesh is Hindi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The official language of Haryana is Hindi, not Punjabi, though Punjabi has second official language status there. The official language of Himachal Pradesh is Hindi, so only statement 2 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Tulu is included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution.
2. English is included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Neither Tulu nor English is included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, which lists 22 scheduled languages. Both statements are false, so neither is correct.

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes Section 6 from Section 7 of the Official Languages Act, 1963?

options.A: Section 6 deals with the Committee of Parliament on Official Language, while Section 7 vests the rule-making power in the Central Government
options.B: Section 6 provides that a translation in Hindi of an Act passed by the Legislature of a State in a language other than Hindi, published in the Official Gazette of the State under the authority of the President, shall be deemed to be the authoritative text thereof in Hindi, while Section 7 provides for the use of Hindi, or the official language of a State, in addition to English, for judgments, decrees or orders of a High Court, on authorisation by the Governor with the previous consent of the President
options.C: Both the Sections deal only with the documents to be issued in both Hindi and English
options.D: Section 6 provides for the use of Hindi in judgments of High Courts, while Section 7 deals with the authoritative Hindi text of State Acts

e: Section 6 of the 1963 Act makes the published Hindi translation of a State Act passed in a language other than Hindi the authoritative Hindi text, while Section 7 provides for use of Hindi or the State official language, in addition to English, for High Court judgments on authorisation by the Governor with the President previous consent.

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes Article 346 from Article 347 of the Constitution?

options.A: Article 346 empowers the President to direct the recognition of a language, while Article 347 deals with communication between the Union and a State
options.B: Both the Articles deal only with the language to be used in the Supreme Court and the High Courts
options.C: Article 346 deals with the development of Hindi, while Article 347 deals with instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage
options.D: Article 346 provides that the language for the time being authorised for use in the Union for its official purposes shall be the official language for communication between the Union and a State, or between one State and another, while Article 347 empowers the President to direct that a language spoken by a substantial proportion of the population of a State shall also be officially recognised for specified purposes

e: Article 346 makes the language authorised for official purposes of the Union the language for communication between the Union and a State and between States, while Article 347 empowers the President to direct official recognition of a language spoken by a substantial proportion of a State population for specified purposes.

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Central Hindi Directorate from the Central Hindi Training Institute?

options.A: The Central Hindi Directorate conducts the correspondence courses in Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya for employees who cannot attend regular classes, while the Central Hindi Training Institute imparts in-service Hindi training to Central Government employees and conducts the Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya examinations
options.B: The Central Hindi Directorate conducts the Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya examinations, while the Central Hindi Training Institute conducts the correspondence courses in those subjects
options.C: Both the bodies are mainly responsible for the translation of codes, manuals and forms of Central Government offices
options.D: Both the bodies function only at the level of Zonal Railways

e: The Central Hindi Directorate conducts the Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya correspondence courses for employees who cannot attend regular classes, while the Central Hindi Training Institute imparts in-service Hindi training to Central Government employees and conducts those examinations.

q: Which one of the following statements relating to the targets prescribed under the Annual Programme for the progressive use of Hindi is FALSE?

options.A: The target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region 'B' is 90 per cent
options.B: The target fixed for noting on files in Hindi is 30 per cent
options.C: The target for issuing the documents specified in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 in both Hindi and English is 55 per cent
options.D: The target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region 'A' is 100 per cent

e: The Annual Programme target for issuing Section 3(3) documents in both Hindi and English is 100 per cent, not 55 per cent, so statement C is false. The Region A correspondence target is 100 per cent, Region B 90 per cent, and the noting target stated is as prescribed in the Programme.

q: Which one of the following statements relating to the Rajbhasha awards of the Department of Official Language and of Indian Railways is FALSE?

options.A: The Acharya Raghuveer Running Shield is awarded to the best (Adarsh) Division in Region 'C'
options.B: The Rajbhasha Kirti Puraskar is awarded for original book writing in Hindi on specified subjects
options.C: The Rail Mantri Rajbhasha Shield is awarded to the Zonal Railway adjudged the best in the implementation of the Official Language Policy
options.D: On Indian Railways, shields and cash awards for excellence in the implementation of the Official Language Policy are given, besides Zonal Railways and Divisions, also to Adarsh stations and Adarsh workshops

e: The Rajbhasha Kirti Puraskar is an award for excellence in Official Language implementation, not for original book writing in Hindi - original book writing is rewarded under the separate Rajbhasha Gaurav Puraskar. The other statements on railway and departmental shields are correct, so B is false.

q: At a check point in a Central Government office, a resolution covered by Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 is presented for despatch in English only. The correct course of action is:

options.A: To despatch it in English, urgency of issue being a valid ground
options.B: To despatch it in English and send the Hindi version a week later
options.C: Not to let the document leave the office unless it is issued in both Hindi and English
options.D: To translate it into Hindi at the check point and despatch the Hindi version alone

e: Check Points are designated precisely to enforce Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963: a resolution covered by that section must not be allowed to leave the office unless it is issued in both Hindi and English.

q: A Central Government office frames certain rules and proposes to issue them in English only, on the ground that they are meant for its officers. Under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the correct position is that the rules are required to be issued in:

options.B: English only, as proposed by the office
options.D: The regional language of the State where the office is located

e: Rules are among the documents listed in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, and must be issued in both Hindi and English, not in English only.

q: A communication between one Ministry of the Central Government and another is sent in the regional language of the State in which the sending Ministry's office is located. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, communications between one Ministry or Department of the Central Government and another may be in:
e: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, communications between one Ministry or Department of the Central Government and another may be in Hindi or English, not in a regional language.

q: A Central Government office issues a communication in Hindi to a person (a member of the public) in Region 'C', without any English translation. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, a communication issued in Hindi to an office or person in Region 'C':

options.A: Needs no accompaniment, Hindi being the Official Language of the Union
options.B: Must be accompanied by its English translation
options.C: Must be sent again in the regional language within a week
options.D: Must first be approved by the Department of Official Language

e: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, a communication in Hindi issued to an office or person in Region C must be accompanied by its English translation.

q: An administrative report of a Central Government office, which is to be laid before both Houses of Parliament, is proposed to be issued in English only. Under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the correct position is that the report is required to be issued in:

options.A: English only, as proposed by the office
options.D: The regional language of the State where the office is located

e: Administrative and other reports required to be laid before both Houses of Parliament are listed in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, and must be issued in both Hindi and English.

q: An employee passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 59 per cent marks. The cash award admissible to him is:
e: Under the Hindi Teaching Scheme cash award slabs for Pragya, marks in the 55 to 59 per cent slab earn Rs 800; 59 per cent falls in that slab.

q: An employee passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 68 per cent marks. The cash award admissible to him is:
e: Under the Hindi Teaching Scheme cash award slabs for Pragya, marks in the 60 to 69 per cent slab earn Rs 1,600; 68 per cent falls in that slab.

q: An employee passes the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 93 per cent marks. In this case:

options.A: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 95 per cent marks
options.B: A cash award is admissible only if he also passes the Hindi stenography examination
options.C: A cash award is admissible to him, the prescribed threshold for the typewriting examination being 90 per cent or more marks
options.D: He becomes entitled to personal pay for a period of 24 months

e: Under the Hindi Teaching Scheme, a cash award for the Hindi typewriting examination is admissible on securing 90 per cent or more marks; 93 per cent crosses that threshold.

q: An employee who was granted personal pay equal to one increment on passing the prescribed Hindi examination claims its continuance in the tenth month after the grant. The correct position is:

options.A: The claim is not in order, personal pay being admissible for a period of 6 months only
options.B: The claim is in order only if the employee passes the examination again
options.C: The claim is not in order, personal pay being admissible only from the thirteenth month
options.D: The claim is in order, personal pay being admissible for a period of 12 months

e: Personal pay equal to one increment granted for passing the prescribed Hindi examination is admissible for 12 months, so a claim in the tenth month is within the admissible period and is in order.

q: An employee aged 42 years, who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi, is nominated for in-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme. The correct position is:

options.A: He must undergo the training, in-service Hindi training being compulsory for an employee who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi and has not attained the age of 45 years
options.B: He is exempt, in-service Hindi training not being compulsory after the age of 40 years
options.C: He must undergo the training only if his office is located in Region 'A'
options.D: He must undergo the training on payment of the prescribed fee

e: In-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is compulsory for an employee who lacks working knowledge of Hindi and has not attained 45 years; at 42 years the employee must undergo it.

q: In a Central Government office, 86 per cent of the staff have acquired working knowledge of Hindi. The correct position regarding notification of the office under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976 is:

options.A: The office cannot be notified, as notification requires more than 90 per cent of the staff to have acquired working knowledge of Hindi
options.B: The office cannot be notified, as notification depends on the total number of staff and not on any proportion
options.C: The office can be notified, the prescribed proportion being 80 per cent or more of the staff having acquired working knowledge of Hindi
options.D: The office can be notified only during Hindi Pakhwada

e: Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976 permits notification of an office where 80 per cent or more of the staff have acquired working knowledge of Hindi; at 86 per cent the office can be notified.

q: An employee does noting and drafting in Hindi of 18,000 words during a year and claims consideration for a cash award under the incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi. The correct position is:

options.A: He is not eligible, the prescribed minimum being 50,000 words in a year
options.B: He becomes eligible for consideration for the cash award, the prescribed minimum being at least 10,000 words of noting and drafting in Hindi in a year
options.C: He is eligible only if he has also passed the Pragya examination with 70 per cent or more marks
options.D: He is eligible only if his office is notified under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976

e: Under the incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi, the prescribed minimum is at least 10,000 words in a year; 18,000 words makes the employee eligible for consideration for the cash award.
